subject: Operational boundaries and subprocessor activation plan for US privacy addendum
messages:
From: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@healthops.com>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai
Cc: security@medtech.io
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Operational scope and telemetry flow for US addendum

Hi Sean —

Thanks again for the demo last week. We are working through the legal diligence for a pilot and the privacy team asked for clarification on a few operational points in the US privacy addendum (CCPA/CPRA). High level asks:

- Confirm whether Redwood will be treated as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA for the services in scope, or if any components should be considered an "operator" (sale/resale risk).
- For telemetry (runtime logs, aggregated traces, and transient cache dumps) we need an onshore fallback option for outage scenarios — can you outline subprocessors you would activate and evidence you can provide for onshore handling?
- Required artifacts: DPA exhibit (signed template), manifest of subprocessors with residency, sample transit encryption proof, and deletion/retention SLAs.

I've attached our RFI spreadsheet and a high-level DataFlow diagram for reference.

[Attachment: HealthOps_RFI_telemetry.xlsx (Excel, 42KB)]
[Attachment: DataFlowDiagram.png (PNG, 180KB)]

Can you confirm feasibility and an approximate turnaround for this evidence? If easier, we can set a 30-minute call next week (would prefer Aug 16).

Appreciate it —
Patricia Gomez
Director, Privacy & Compliance — HealthOps
patricia.gomez@healthops.com

---

From: sean_gallagher <sean_gallagher@redwood.ai>
To: Patricia Gomez <patricia.gomez@healthops.com>
Cc: laura_bennett@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational scope and telemetry flow for US addendum

Patricia —

Thanks for the clear list and the diagram. Short answers up front:

- Redwood's standard position is to act as a "service provider" (we process customer data on the customer's behalf) for the hosted and dedicated modes you reviewed. We do not resell customer data and our standard DPA explicitly disclaims "sale" classification.

- That said, there are narrow operational cases (transient telemetry used for routing/failover) where we treat a small set of telemetry signals as operationally necessary. We can provide a carve‑out description that remains consistent with Service Provider obligations and does not expand to a resale use.

- Onshore fallback: we maintain a documented subprocessor activation playbook. For HealthOps we can commit to three onshore fallback subprocessors (two preferred cloud partners + one managed ops partner). We'll provide residency attestations and a signed addendum for activation conditions.

What we'll deliver within the requested timeline if you confirm:
1) Signed DPA exhibit (redwood-dpa-exhibit.pdf).
2) Subprocessor manifest with residency and activation clauses.
3) Sample transit encryption proof and log-retention excerpt.
4) Onshore fallback activation playbook (conditions and SLAs).

Proposed timeline: 5–7 business days after we get a short list of which telemetry types you need onshore and whether you require continuous residency or just activation under incident conditions.

If Aug 16 works, I'd like to include Laura (legal ops) and Grace (product security) — can you send a calendar invite for a 30-min slot?

Best,
Sean Gallagher
Enterprise Account Executive — Redwood Inference
sean_gallagher@redwood.ai | +1 (415) 555-0192
[Attachment: redwood-dpa-exhibit.pdf (PDF, 58KB)]

From: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
To: sean_gallagher@redwood.ai, grace_oconnor@redwood.ai, karthik_iyer@redwood.ai
Date: Fri, 14 Aug 2026 15:22:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Operational scope and telemetry flow for US addendum

Sean / team —

Picking up from Sean's note with a suggested internal posture and deliverables. Quoting Patricia's ask for clarity:

> - Confirm whether Redwood will be treated as a "service provider" under CCPA/CPRA for the services in scope
> - Onshore fallback option for telemetry, list of subprocessors and evidence

Internal position (recommended):
- Primary classification: Service Provider for all data processed for HealthOps under the hosted/dedicated offerings. We should provide an explicit paragraph in the exhibit that calls out non-resale / no-sale commitments.
- Telemetry carve-out: Provide a narrowly scoped technical definition (fields and retention windows) for the telemetry signals used solely for health/failover. Make clear these signals are not used for advertising, monetization, or profiling.
- Onshore fallback: Offer activation-based residency (i.e., subprocessors that are activated only under incident/failover). For HealthOps we can offer to attest to three named onshore subprocessors and a contractual obligation to move relevant telemetry to onshore storage within X hours of activation.

Docs to produce (we'll own these, estimate 5 business days once we confirm telemetry types):
- Signed DPA + addendum paragraph (final text for their counsel).
- Subprocessor manifest with residency and activation conditions.
- Sample TLS/TCP config export to demonstrate transit encryption.
- Retention/deletion excerpt (log retention table).

Risks / asks for product/security:
- Grace: confirm if the KV-cache dump (used during node restarts) contains identifiers that require broader residency guarantees. If yes, we must treat that as a higher-sensitivity telemetry type.
- Karthik: can you prepare the activation playbook stub and an estimated SLA for moving telemetry onshore (e.g., 6 hours vs 24 hours)?

I'll draft language for the DPA exhibit and circulate for quick legal review. Sean — once Patricia confirms the telemetry list, we should be ready for the Aug 16 call.

Thanks,
Laura Bennett
Sr. Counsel, Commercial Contracts — Redwood Inference
laura_bennett@redwood.ai

Subject: Re: Operational scope and telemetry flow for US addendum

Sean / team —

Appreciate the fast turnaround and clear next steps. A few clarifications before the call:

1) Telemetry list: please treat the following as requiring onshore activation: runtime error logs (stack traces), KV-cache dumps (transient), and aggregated latency traces. System metrics (CPU/memory) do not require onshore handling.

2) Sale classification: our counsel will need a short paragraph in the exhibit explicitly stating Redwood does not "sell" HealthOps data and that telemetry types listed above are only processed for operation and troubleshooting.

3) DocuSign: please send the finalized DPA exhibit via DocuSign. We need signatures from both parties before any pilot data ingestion.

4) Evidence: attach a sample residency attestation for the three named onshore subprocessors (company + state of residency) and a short retention table for the telemetry types above. If you have a playbook PDF, include that as well.

I've attached an updated SOW for the pilot — it references activation windows (we propose 12 hours) and an acceptance checkpoint after ingesting test traffic.

[Attachment: HealthOps_SOW_v2.pdf (PDF, 120KB)]

Looking forward to the call on Aug 16 at 10:00 PT.

Best,
Patricia Gomez
Director, Privacy & Compliance — HealthOps
